answer: Trust-graph routing curtails Sybil attacks by bounding payment flow along cryptographically signed peer paths. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locking scarce collateral in bilateral channels per identity. When telemetry agents report a cool zephyr over a citrus grove or moisture tension along an orchard vine, throughput depends on topological bottlenecks rather than identity tallies. However, this barrier creates liquidity lockups and isolates legitimate new entrants.
